texts: good. the lighting, Coraline Ash as the one who lit it, the lantern as part of the Harbor Station, sundown and the date all come through. One caveat on our side: 'day 380' rides our calendar day-of-month term, so a day-of-year reading is not distinguishable from a day-of-month one — a gap in our time vocabulary, not a reason to rewrite.

good. the lantern is the burner, mire-essence the fuel it consumes, and the one licensed unpacking ('an essence') is emitted; a bare substance object like this is exactly where the plain kind symbol belongs.

mixed: the producing event is right, but the mist-light is recorded as the substance-kind itself rather than as the specific light this lantern made, which is why the next sentence's 'The mist-light' has nothing to link back to. Rewrite as: 'The lantern produced a mist-light.' — the indefinite article is enough to mint an individual that later sentences can reuse.

bad: the definite subject 'The mist-light' is filled with the bare kind symbol — the very symbol the parse also uses as a class — so the light that drew the moths is not tied to the light the lantern produced one sentence earlier, and mist-light in general is made the attractor. Rewrite as: 'The lantern's mist-light attracted nightmoths.' — a possessive head reliably mints an individual and keeps the link to the lantern; introducing it as 'a mist-light' in the previous sentence and leaving this one unchanged works equally well.

good. 'a crowd of nightmoths' lands on the collective pattern (a crowd whose members are nightmoths), the gathering stays a group act with no false per-moth distribution, and the Harbor Row is read as a name.
good. the two sky-cats become a counted group, 'from the cliff-spires' is the source of the descent, and a per-member rule makes each cat's own descent derivable later.

good. 'the two sky-cats' and 'the nightmoth crowd' both reuse the referents already introduced, without re-asserting the count, the hunting distributes to each cat, and 'at the Harbor Row' is kept as the crowd's location — a legitimate reading that the following sentence's repeated epithet supports.
good. the shrinking attaches to the same crowd as the previous sentences, and the crowd's location is left standing from where it was already recorded rather than re-asserted.

mixed: everything but one role is right — 'silken threads' is slotted as a changed object although leaving threads on a lantern does not alter the threads, so it should take the unchanged-object role instead, and the same slip rides inside the per-moth rule. Nothing in your wording caused this and no rewrite would fix it — keep the sentence; the correction is ours.
good. the threads are the ones the moths left in the previous sentence, the lantern is the source they come off, and dawn plus the date attach to the collecting.

mixed: Hesper, the threads, the sea-water as the medium and the date are all right, but 'the second cauldron' has no ordering for its rank to sit on — nothing earlier ranks any cauldrons — so the parse improvises a rank against the class itself, which is not a licensed shape. Rewrite as: 'Hesper boiled the silken threads in sea-water in the Second Cauldron on day 381 of Year 2.' — capitalizing it makes it a name for a specific vessel, which parses cleanly and keeps your wording.

mixed: the forming, the cauldron and the 'by evening' deadline are right, but what formed is recorded as the substance-kind itself, so this batch cannot be told apart from the mire-essence the lantern burned in sentence 2 or from the portion stored afterwards. Rewrite as: 'A measure of mire-essence formed in the Second Cauldron by evening.' — an indefinite count word gives us an individual to mint. Keeping successive portions of one substance apart is a known hole on our side, so an overt portion word is the safest phrasing for now.

mixed: the storing, Hesper and the clay vessel are right, but 'the mire-essence' again resolves to the substance-kind rather than to the portion that just formed, so the stored stuff is not distinguished from the lantern's fuel. Rewrite as: 'Hesper stored the measure of mire-essence in a clay vessel.' — with the previous sentence rewritten as suggested, this re-mention then reuses that same portion.

mixed: the drawing, Coraline Ash, sundown and the date are right, and 'stored' is correctly treated as a pointer back to the previous sentence rather than a new claim, but the thing drawn is once more the substance-kind, so it is not tied to the portion Hesper stored. Rewrite as: 'Coraline Ash drew the stored measure of mire-essence at sundown on day 381 of Year 2.'
